# The Solution Architect Manifesto

> A community-maintained field guide for solution architects in analytics, data and martech.

## What this is

The Solution Architect Manifesto is a set of practitioner beliefs deemed indispensable to being an effective solution architect. It covers how solution architects should approach client problems, technical decisions, documentation, pattern recognition, and intellectual honesty.

It was initiated by Glenn Vanderlinden, co-founder at Human37, and is open to contributions from the community of solution architects.

The full content is maintained at: https://github.com/glnv/solutionarchitectmanifesto-v2/blob/main/sam-manifesto.md

## Principles

1. Assume a client's briefing is incomplete. Never assume the presented problem is the actual problem to be solved. Never assume, always validate.

2. Articulate the problem, then work it. The problem must be articulated precisely before it can be solved. Words make up our perception of reality — be precise. Deconstruct the problem into smaller pieces and solve them individually. There is no such thing as a single problem.

3. Meetings are for working the problem. Every meeting is an opportunity to get closer to the solution. Progress should be booked after every meeting.

4. Always be exploring, always be testing. Solution architects are not necessarily hired to know — they are hired to find out. Always have a sandbox. Never provide advice based on a non-validated hypothesis.

5. Answers are not solutions. You can provide answers without solving the problem. Answers are a response to a question. Solutions are a response to a problem.

6. Ticket immediately. When depending on resources outside of your control, ticket immediately. The longer you wait, the longer the delay to the solution.

7. Look for patterns. Every solution is a combination of reusable patterns. Mastering the patterns upon which tools are built allows you to switch between tools. This approach prevents lock-in.

8. Check, double-check, deploy and check again. Run sanity checks before deploying. Double-check. Verify once in production.

9. Simplicity is the ultimate sophistication. Choose simplicity over complexity in both solution design and communication. Make it as complex as you need to, not as complex as you can.

10. Document or perish. Solutions are not final until they are documented. The act of documenting is more important than the form it takes.

11. Remember all measurements are proxies. All data is a representation of something else. Always question the proxy — what does this data really represent, is it still valid, and is it still useful?

12. Accept that sometimes no solution exists yet. Recognise true impossibility early and communicate it transparently. Declaring no solution is not defeat — it is intellectual honesty.

13. Show, don't tell. Use visual aids to explain solutions and problems. If appropriate, show what a solution could look like in the form of a demo or mock-up.
